summary: FCB Financial Holdings is a Florida-based regional bank with supply-chain fragility centered on real estate lending and deposit stickiness. Its financial inputs (deposits, wholesale funding) are relatively diversified, but single-state geographic concentration amplifies credit risk. Near-term stability depends on Florida's economy and interest rate trajectory.

inputs.concentration: moderate - retail & commercial depositors, FDIC insured cap limits flight risk
inputs.fragility: low currently, but could become high if rate competition intensifies

inputs.concentration: low - multiple sources (FHLB, brokered deposits, fed funds)

inputs.whyNeeded: Core asset class generating interest income
inputs.concentration: high - over 80% CRE & residential within Florida
inputs.fragility: high - single-state exposure amplifies downturn risk

chokepoints.why: Dominant asset class; a housing or tourism downturn would directly impair loan portfolio
Profitability hinges on spread between deposit costs and loan yields; inverted yield curve squeezes it

bearCase: Florida recession, hurricane catastrophe, or housing crash triggers sharp credit losses; deposit outflows & NIM contraction force capital raise or dilution.
